rationale: The QoI is peak vorticity (a spatial velocity-gradient reduction), but the substrate can only reduce fields the case actually wrote via volAverage/min/max/volIntegrate — it cannot compute ∂v/∂x−∂u/∂y, so the target quantity is fundamentally unextractable by this instrument.

The QoI is a vorticity-based sub-domain circulation ratio, but the substrate can only reduce (volAverage/min/max/volIntegrate) existing written fields over the whole domain — vorticity is never written and sub-domain integration is unsupported, so the instrument cannot produce the quantity at all.

The in-envelope laminar CFD directly and reliably computes min(Ux), but mesh-independence is explicitly not claimed (corner vortices under-resolved at Re=1000) and the statistic is an admitted indirect proxy for secondary-vortex emergence, so a finer solve or real experiment could still correct the…

The instrument's canonical vocabulary has no profile_amplitude parameter and its scalar lid_velocity cannot express the spatially-varying cosine lid boundary condition the hypothesis requires, so the builder halts and the bimodal-vs-uniform comparison cannot be modeled at all.

The double-Gaussian spatially-varying lid profile requires a codedFixedValue boundary condition and non-canonical parameters (profile_sigma, profile_peak_velocity) that the case builder cannot synthesize, so every run fails at case construction and no QoI is produced.

The substrate cannot build the central-obstacle geometry (non-canonical parameters halt the builder) nor extract enstrophy (a two-step vorticity/squared-magnitude derivation outside the single-operation QoI path), so it cannot model this experiment at all.

The 64x64 mesh at Re=1000 is marginally under-resolved versus the Ghia et al. 129x129 benchmark, so the direct-read min(Ux) is a reliable trend estimate but its absolute value carries unconfirmed mesh-dependence, and the trust-critical -0.35 threshold sits exactly where that error bites.
